newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia seeks broader U.S. owner base - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Nokia seeks broader U.S. owner base - CFO.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy is targeting a U.S. shareholder base of 200,000 and wants to expand its ownership base in Finland, its chief financial officer Olli-Pekka Kallasvuo said on Friday.

Some 60,000 investors in the United States currently own Nokia shares or American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) and it has about 27,000 shareholders in Finland, he said at a seminar on listings for Finnish firms in the United States.
"In the U.S., it is not enough to have owners only in New York and Boston...it doesn't give enough support. We target 200,000 shareholders in the U.S.," he told the seminar.
"It is also very important to be able to increase the number of our shareholders in Finland," he later told reporters.

Most U.S. and Finnish holders of Nokia shares are private, although institutional investors hold large chunks of its stock, noted Kallasvuo, who was recently appointed executive vice president of Nokia's Americas division.
He said the number of Nokia shareholders was increasing, and Nokia was working hard on investor relations to boost this both in Finland and the United States.
